claims.text: Increasing the Al content of an AlNbTiZr medium-entropy-alloy coating to approximately 10 at.% will promote formation of a mixed Nb2Zr6O17 and ZrO2 oxide scale.
The approximately 10 at.% Al coating will form the mixed oxide scale during high-temperature steam oxidation under accident conditions.
The oxide scale formed by the high-Al coating will be dense.
The oxide scale formed by the high-Al coating will be adherent.
The dense oxide scale will act as a diffusion barrier that reduces oxygen penetration.
Higher Al content favors formation of stable, slow-growing oxide phases during high-temperature exposure.
Impeded oxygen diffusion will reduce the oxidation rate of the underlying zirconium substrate under LOCA conditions.
The 10 at.% Al coating will significantly reduce oxidation weight gain relative to a lower-Al coating.
The 10 at.% Al coating will have a lower high-temperature steam oxidation rate than a lower-Al coating.
The high-Al coating will maintain coating adhesion and overall material integrity during LOCA-simulated oxidation.
The modified coating will retain mechanical properties needed for normal reactor operation.
The modified coating will retain suitable hydrophobic properties for normal reactor operation.
Uncoated zirconium-alloy cladding or cladding with a standard low-Al coating undergoes rapid oxidation under LOCA conditions.
Lower-Al AlNbTiZr coatings form less protective oxide scales than an approximately 10 at.% Al coating.
AlNbTiZr coatings with approximately 10 at.% Al can be deposited on zirconium-alloy substrates by RF magnetron co-sputtering.
LOCA-relevant steam oxidation conditions span approximately 800 °C to 1600 °C.
The coating's benefits outside the stated temperature range or after substantial changes in overall composition have not been established.
The optimal Al threshold and interactions with the other alloy constituents remain uncertain.
It is uncertain whether the modified coating will satisfy long-term mechanical and corrosion requirements under cyclic reactor conditions.
